title: A constant oxygen-use law fits all six A20 bins in 2012 and 2021 at 5% tracer tolerance when old components are allowed
abstract: We tested whether the failed finite-grid common-law fits on A20 exclude all constant oxygen-use laws. We used GLODAPv2.2023, paired CFC-12 and SF6, exact age bounds under interpolated source histories, and a continuous search over nonnegative rate and preformed AOU. At 5% tracer tolerance and a 200-year age limit, one law fitted all six matched A20 bins in both 2012 and 2021 with nonnegative component oxygen. One fit has rate 2.91814 umol/kg/year, preformed AOU 9.80510 umol/kg, and oldest active component age 77.31 years. A 50-year limit, 2% tracer tolerance, or a 100 umol/kg component oxygen floor excluded common-law fits at A20 in the tested model. A22 allowed a 50-year fit with a 100 umol/kg floor at 5%, but not at 2%. The method tests the full continuous parameter domain and audits explicit spectra. It closes the finite-grid gap but does not establish a ventilation cause. Results depend on source saturation, the partial-pressure mixing approximation, local source oxygen, age support and error tolerance. External records and spectra remain outside the bundle; retrieval and analysis code are included.

display.caption: Common-law fits depend on age support, tracer tolerance and the component oxygen floor. Exclusions are continuous numerical feasibility results under the stated source model.

citations.reason: We extend the finite parameter-grid test to a continuous physical search and find a complete A20 fit.
The small inverse-Gaussian age change is not a shape-free bound on mean-age change. Our level tests do not establish a complete ventilation-only explanation.
Motivates tests that do not assign a causal share from a fitted tracer age.
